policy: Human-reviewed authoritative public pages; fixed offline references, not live fetching or a guarantee of current rules. Each note verifies ONLY its stated claim. No source here verifies a rent quote, footfall, platform fee, market share, restaurant demand or suitable lease.

sources.title: Registration for VAT
sources.supported_claim: The FTA gives a mandatory VAT registration threshold of AED 375,000 in taxable supplies and imports over the preceding 12 months, or expected in the next 30 days, for the resident-business situation described on this page.
sources.limitations: Registration exceptions and non-resident rules vary; this is not a determination that the restaurant is already registered or liable.

sources.title: Corporate Tax — General Guide
sources.supported_claim: The general UAE Corporate Tax rates in the FTA guide are 0% on taxable income up to AED 375,000 and 9% on taxable income above that level.
sources.limitations: This is taxable INCOME, not turnover and not a general CT registration threshold. Eligibility, exemptions, and current rules must be checked with FTA.

sources.title: Corporate Tax Registration
sources.supported_claim: Persons subject to UAE Corporate Tax are directed to apply for a Corporate Tax Registration Number under the applicable FTA registration rules.
sources.limitations: Which rules apply depends on entity type; a tax professional should confirm the restaurant's obligations and deadlines.

sources.title: For Food Traders and Establishments
sources.supported_claim: Dubai Municipality publishes Food Code materials and food-establishment, transportation, food activity permit and approval requirements.
sources.limitations: This source does not establish approval for a particular site, equipment layout, venting specification, timeline or landlord arrangement.

sources.title: Food safety
sources.supported_claim: The UAE Government Portal identifies ADAFSA as the food-safety authority in Abu Dhabi and the relevant municipal authorities for food safety in Dubai.
sources.limitations: This does not specify permits, approval timing or suitability of any individual kitchen in Abu Dhabi.

sources.title: Jumeirah Lakes Towers guide
sources.supported_claim: The destination guide describes JLT as mixed offices, apartments and hotels, restaurants at tower bases and a walkable lake-and-park layout with metro access.
sources.limitations: A tourism description is NOT verified pedestrian counts, restaurant sales, current availability, rental pricing, delivery demand or site-specific ROI.

sources.publisher: Experience Abu Dhabi — official destination website
sources.title: Al Zahiyah neighbourhood guide
sources.supported_claim: The destination guide describes Al Zahiyah (Tourist Club Area) as an established, centrally located Abu Dhabi neighbourhood near the Corniche and main business district.
sources.limitations: It does NOT verify rents, achievable average ticket, local restaurant demand, competitive saturation or suitability for a specific first branch.
